analyst: QSB Tower V1.3 dormant import process

detected_kernel.name: QSB Kernel
detected_kernel.principle: Models are workers. QSB is the kernel.
detected_kernel.cognitive_upgrade_notes: COGNITIVE_47_README.md describes semantic memory, belief engine, reflection engine additions

uses_old_qsb_skyscraper_paths.detail: All core files hardcode ROOT = Path('/vaults/nvme0/qsb_skyscraper'). continuity_core.py, belief_core.py, and symbolic_core.py all resolve database and state file paths relative to that ROOT.

uses_old_executive_penthouse_assumptions.detail: executive/penthouse.py imports from workers.router.router, memory.memory_core, memory.semantic_memory, departments.department_core, missions.mission_core, bus.lift_core, knowledge.graph_core — all old skyscraper module paths. It calls router.health() which likely invokes Ollama. It uses sys.path manipulation against the old skyscraper ROOT.
uses_old_executive_penthouse_assumptions.interactive_loop: penthouse.py contains an interactive input() loop — must NOT be run in tower context

may_call_local_models.detail: penthouse.py instantiates QSBRouter which calls Ollama locally. The kernel core files themselves (kernel_core.py, axiom_core.py, etc.) do NOT call models — only the executive/penthouse.py orchestrator does.
may_call_local_models.kernel_core_files_alone: kernel_core.py and sub-cores do not directly call any LLM or Ollama API

may_write_memory_or_state.detail: If instantiated, the following would write to old skyscraper paths:
writes: continuity_core.py writes /vaults/nvme0/qsb_skyscraper/kernel/continuity_state.json on every boot_check() call
identity_core.py may write identity.json if file is absent
may_write_memory_or_state.mitigation: The dormant adapter reads only identity.json and continuity_state.json as static JSON — it does NOT instantiate any kernel class

compatibility_risks.detail: All core modules resolve paths against /vaults/nvme0/qsb_skyscraper. If instantiated in tower context they would write to the wrong vault.
compatibility_risks.mitigation: Do not instantiate. Read identity.json and continuity_state.json as static JSON files only.

compatibility_risks.detail: penthouse.py requires workers.router.router, memory.memory_core, departments.department_core, etc. — none of which exist in the new tower.
compatibility_risks.mitigation: Do not run executive/penthouse.py. It is imported as a reference artifact only.

compatibility_risks.detail: BeliefCore.__init__, SymbolicLogicCore.__init__, and ContinuityCore.boot_check() all write to disk on construction. Instantiating QSBKernelCore would trigger all of these.
compatibility_risks.mitigation: Dormant adapter must never call QSBKernelCore(). Read only.

compatibility_risks.detail: penthouse.py contains while True: msg = input('Penthouse> ') — running it would block the tower process.
compatibility_risks.mitigation: penthouse.py is stored as reference source only. Never imported or executed.

compatibility_risks.detail: penthouse.py calls router.health() which expects Ollama running locally.
compatibility_risks.mitigation: penthouse.py is not executed. Kernel sub-cores are read-only in dormant mode.

compatibility_risks.detail: Before the kernel can be activated in the new tower, all ROOT path references must be rewritten from /vaults/nvme0/qsb_skyscraper to /vaults/nvme0/qsb_tower_v1.
compatibility_risks.mitigation: Path rebase is a required step in the future activation phase — NOT performed during dormant import.

notes: The kernel sub-cores (kernel_core.py + sub-cores) contain no network calls and no external model calls.
All side-effects come from file I/O to old skyscraper paths — avoidable by not instantiating.
The dormant adapter must only read identity.json and continuity_state.json as static JSON.
penthouse.py must be stored as reference source only — never imported or run.
Before activation: paths must be rebased, old skyscraper imports must be mapped to new tower equivalents.
Activation requires explicit operator decision and is NOT part of this import phase.
